rationale: C15 is a highly plausible direct drafting template. It uses the same multi-airline dispute structure, the same employee representative (International Association of Machinists), six of the child’s seven named carriers, and the distinctive plural operative phrase applying the status-quo requirement to “any of the said carriers or their employees.” The child largely preserves C15’s full recital-and-operative sequence while updating the carrier list. C05 and C09 are close contemporaneous Eastern Air Lines orders with nearly identical machinery, but their single-carrier and different-union formulations are less specifically matched to the child.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Eastern Air Lines, Inc., Trans World Airlines, Inc., United Air Lines, Inc., Northwest Airlines, Inc., Northeast Airlines, Inc., Capital Airlines, Inc., and National Airlines, Inc., carriers
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Capital Airlines, Inc., National Airlines, Inc., Northwest Airlines, Inc., Trans World Airlines, Inc., United Airlines, Inc., Eastern Airlines, Inc., carriers
shared_material.explanation: The directives concern nearly the same enumerated group of airlines; the child retains six carriers and adds Northeast Airlines.

shared_material.parent_excerpt: certain of their employees represented by the International Association of Machinists, a labor organization
shared_material.explanation: This dispute-party formulation is effectively identical, including the same union.

shared_material.explanation: The distinctive plural status-quo provision is reproduced verbatim.
